<reason>Both sides built genuine, well-grounded cases and answered pressure questions directly with proper A1/A2 formatting. CON's verification/asymmetry argument (bolstered by the accurate observation that major-power holdouts undermined the landmine/cluster bans) was consistently strong and never fully neutralized. But CON's own answer to PRO's pressure question—proposing mandatory human review certified via audit logs—handed PRO the decisive closing move: that a "certification you must pass is a prohibition on failing it," and that software-generated audit logs are exactly as spoofable as the "meaningful control" CON called unverifiable. CON's closing reasserted the positive/negative verification distinction but never actually rebutted the log-symmetry point, leaving PRO's sharpest blow unanswered at the end of the debate. PRO's case also suffered real execution costs (two clipped over-length speeches losing final weighing content), which keeps the margin modest rather than dominant, but the substantive trap sprung in the final exchange was the most consequential unresolved move in the debate.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's closing (B5.1–B5.5), which shows CON's own proposed "certification" alternative is functionally identical to the banned category ("meaningful human review before engagement"), and that CON's audit-log verification is just as vulnerable to the firmware-toggle problem CON used to attack prohibition—an argument CON's final speech never directly answers.</best_rebuttal>
